title: Count Unit Squares to Determine Area
goal: I can count unit squares in rows and columns to find area, and name it with the right square unit.
catchAll: Count the squares row by row. Then name the area with its unit: square centimeters, square feet …

teacher.def: number of unit squares needed to cover the INSIDE of a shape or region
a square that is 1 unit tall and 1 unit wide

glossary.row: a line of squares going across
glossary.column: a line of squares going up and down
glossary.square foot: a square 1 foot long on each side
glossary.square centimeter: a square 1 centimeter long on each side

screens.title: Rows and columns
text: Squares in a rectangle line up in rows (across) and columns (up and down).
This rectangle has 4 rows. Each row has 5 squares.
screens.caption: 4 rows of 5 unit squares

screens.title: Count by rows
text: Then count on by 5 for each row: 5, 10, 15, 20.

screens.title: Squares can have real sizes
text: A unit square can be 1 centimeter, 1 inch, 1 foot or 1 meter on each side.
Name the area with the unit: 6 squares that are 1 foot on each side cover 6 square feet.
screens.caption: Each square is 1 square foot. Area: 6 square feet.

item.prompt: Each square is 1 centimeter long on each side. A shape is covered by 8 of them. What is its area?

options.why: Centimeters measure a length. Area is in square centimeters.
The squares are 1 centimeter on each side, not 1 foot.

screens.title: Shapes that are not rectangles
text: Some shapes are not rectangles. Count only the squares inside the shape.
Count row by row and add: 3 + 3 + 1 = 7 square units.
screens.caption: Count only the shaded squares.

item.prompt: What is the area of the shaded shape in square units?
hints: Count the shaded squares in each row. Leave out the empty ones.

watch.takeaway: Count every square inside the shape once, row by row, and name the area with its square unit.

steps.say: Problem: find the area of the rectangle.
Step 1: Count the squares in one row.
Step 3: Count on by 5 for each row: 5, 10, 15, 20.
Step 4: Name the unit: 20 square units.

why.prompt: Why can we count on by 5?

options.why: There are 4 rows. Each row has 5 squares.
Odd or even does not matter. Each row has 5.

why.yes: Yes! Equal rows let us count on by the same number.

examples.title: Example B: a shape on squared paper

steps.say: Problem: what is the area of the shaded shape?
Step 1: Count the shaded squares in the top row: 3.
Step 2: The middle row has 4 shaded squares.
Step 3: The bottom row has 1 shaded square. The empty squares are not part of the shape.
Step 5: The area is 8 square units.
Problem: a rug is covered by squares that are 1 foot on each side. What is its area?
Step 1: Each square is 1 square foot.
Step 3: The rug covers 12 square feet.

items.prompt: How do you decide which unit to use for area?

options.text: Use the size of one unit square.

options.why: The unit depends on the squares used.
Corners do not tell the unit.

hints: What size is each square?
show: If each square is 1 inch on each side, the area is in square inches.
items.yes: Yes! The unit square decides the unit.

items.prompt: A garden has 3 rows of planter boxes, 6 boxes in each row. Each box is 1 square foot. What is the area of the garden?

hints: Count the boxes in one row, then add the rows.

items.prompt: Why do we count row by row?

options.text: So no square is skipped or counted twice.

options.why: Columns work too. Counting in order keeps track.
The way you count does not change the area.

hints: Think about keeping track.
show: Counting in order keeps track of every square.

sections.heading: What your child is learning
sections.text: Your child counts unit squares in rows and columns to find area, including shapes that are not rectangles, and names the area with its unit (square centimeters, square inches, square feet, square meters).

sections.heading: Try it with real things
list: Measure a book cover with 1-inch sticky squares and count them.
Draw shapes on graph paper and count the squares inside.

sections.heading: Questions to ask
list: How many squares are in one row?
What size is each square, so what unit do we use?

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Counting the empty squares on the paper as part of the shape.
Writing feet instead of square feet.
Adding one row and one column instead of counting every square.
